blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
LiDAR point clouds of humans are extremely expensive to collect and annotate, thus represent a scarce resource that hinders the development of human analysis using this modality.
To alleviate this scarcity, prior work relies on simulated human LiDAR, but such samples do not fully reflect the geometry and sensing characteristics of real observations.
In contrast, we introduce HuLiGen , a generative model that generates human LiDAR point clouds from a parametric body model, using a point transformer trained with a flow-matching objective. We show that our generated point clouds are closer to the real capture distribution.
Using HuLiGen to generate synthetic data, we propose a synthetic-only pretraining scheme for LiDAR-based HPE that achieves state-of-the-art performance, with even larger gains in low-annotation and low-data regimes, where MPJPE is reduced by up to 50%. Code, models and generated samples are available at https://github.com/valeoai/HuLiGen .
blocks.zh:

为了缓解这种稀缺性,先前的工作依赖于模拟的人类LiDAR,但这种样本不能充分反映真实观测的几何和感知特征.
相形之下,我们引入了HuLiGen(HuliGen),一种从参数体模型中生成人类LiDAR点云的基因模型,使用一个被训练出有流相匹配目标的点变器. 我们显示我们产生的点云 更接近真实的捕捉分布

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
3D human pose estimation (HPE) is an important task for human-centric perception in embodied systems. Accurate estimation of human body pose can provide fine-grained cues for pedestrian behavior understanding and intention prediction [ 32 ] , as well as trajectory forecasting [ 2 , 15 ] , which are important for collision avoidance and interaction-aware motion planning [ 28 ] .
The geometric nature of LiDAR makes it particularly attractive for these applications, but also introduces a fundamental bottleneck: human LiDAR data with accurate 3D pose annotations remains difficult to obtain at scale.
blocks.zh:
3D人类姿势估计(HPE)是所体现系统中以人类为中心的认知的一项重要任务. 准确估计人体姿势可以为行人行为理解和意向预测提供精细的提示 [32],以及轨迹预测 [2,15],这对于避免相撞和互动意识运动规划[28]非常重要.
LiDAR的几何性质使得它对这些应用特别有吸引力,但也引入了一个根本性的瓶颈:人类有准确的3D的LiDAR数据在规模上仍然难以得到说明.

blocks.en:
Constructing such datasets requires substantial annotation effort. LiDAR points on humans are sparse, viewpoint dependent, and frequently affected by self-occlusion and external occlusions, while accurate pose supervision typically requires synchronized motion-capture systems, additional cameras or inertial sensors.
Recent datasets such as SLOPER4D [ 7 ] and the Waymo Open Dataset (WOD) [ 39 ] provide real-world point clouds together with human pose annotations which help the progress in LiDAR-based human pose estimation.
Nevertheless, the available data still covers only a limited range of human poses and body shapes.
For example, SLOPER4D contains more than 100K LiDAR frames but only 12 recorded subjects, while WOD provides approximately 10K object frames with 3D keypoint annotations.
In contrast, large-scale human body-model repositories such as AMASS [ 24 ] , provide a much richer diversity of human poses and body configurations, but lack corresponding LiDAR observations.
blocks.zh:
建立这种数据集需要大量的说明。 对人类的LiDAR指点很少,视线依附,经常会受自闭和外闭的影响,而准确的外闭一般需要同步的运动捕捉系统,额外的相机或惯性传感器.
最近的数据集,如SLOPER4D [7]和Waymo Open Dataset (WOD) [39] 提供了现实世界点云,以及人类的姿势说明,这有助于基于LiDAR的人类姿势估计的进展.
然而,现有数据仍然只涵盖有限的人类外形和身体形状。
例如,SLOPER4D包含有超过100K LiDAR帧,但只有12个被记录的主题,而WOD则提供了约10K对象帧并带有3D键点说明.
相形之下,AMASS等大型人体模型寄存器[24]提供了更丰富的人类姿势和身体配置的多样性,但缺乏相应的LiDAR观测.

blocks.en:
To compensate for the limited amount and diversity of annotated human LiDAR data, a common strategy is to generate synthetic samples from parametric body models using ray casting [ 3 , 40 , 35 , 42 ] . However, the realism of these samples is limited by the manually defined rendering process [ 25 , 49 ] .
Real LiDAR observations depend not only on the underlying body geometry, but also on clothing and surface variations, viewpoint, range, sensor configuration and measurement uncertainty.
Modeling these effects requires explicit assumptions and hand-crafted noise or sensor models.
blocks.zh:
为了补偿附加注释的人类LiDAR数据数量和多样性有限,一个共同的战略是利用射线铸造[3,40,35,42]从参数体模型中生成合成样品. 然而,这些样本的现实性受到人工定义的渲染过程[25,49]的限制.
真实的LiDAR观测不仅依赖于地基地体几何,还依赖于衣物和地表变化,视角,范围,传感器配置和测量不确定性.
模拟这些效果需要明确的假设和手工制作的噪音或传感器模型.

blocks.en: In this work, we explore a different paradigm: rather than explicitly simulating the interaction of the LiDAR with the body model to obtain the point cloud, we learn it directly from real lidar observations. Given real human point clouds paired with corresponding body models, we train a conditional flow-matching model that acts as a learned LiDAR renderer, modeling how a given human pose and shape is observed by a real sensor. This formulation learns real LiDAR characteristics such as sparsity, viewpoint- and range-dependent sampling and uncertainty. It can also capture deviations from the underlying body model caused by clothing, hair and other surface variations (see Fig. 1 ). Finally, it decouples pose diversity from sensor realism: large-scale mocap data provides diverse human poses, while real LiDAR data defines how these poses are observed.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们探索了一个不同的范式:我们不是明确模拟LiDAR与身体模型的相互作用以获得点云,而是直接从真正的lidar观测中学习. 由于真人点云与相应的身体模型对接,我们训练出一种有条件的相通相配模型,作为有学问的LiDAR渲染器,模拟一个真人传感器如何观察到一个给定的人类姿势和形状. 这种配方学习了真实的LiDAR特性,如相扑性,视距和测距依赖的采样和不确定性等. 它还能捕捉出由服装,发型等表面变化而导致的与基础身体模型的偏差(见图一. 最后,它从感官现实主义中去除杂交呈现出多样性:大规模摩卡普数据提供了多样的人类姿势,而真正的LiDAR数据则定义了这些姿势是如何被观察到的.

blocks.en:
Once trained, the model can generate LiDAR observations for previously unseen poses, allowing us to leverage existing large-scale mocap datasets with diverse poses and body configurations to generate sensor-specific human point clouds.
Beyond evaluating generation quality using standard generative metrics, we further assess the generated point clouds on the downstream task of 3D human pose estimation. We show that pretraining a pose estimator on generated human LiDAR samples, followed by finetuning on real data, significantly improves performance in both full-data and low-data regimes. Experiments with different fractions of the real training set further show that our generated data can compensate for limited labeled real data.
blocks.zh:
该模型经过培训后,可以生成LiDAR观测结果,用于前所未见的外观,使我们能够利用现有的有多种外观和身体配置的大型摩克数据组来生成传感器特有的人点云.
除了利用标准的基因计量来评估生成质量之外,我们还进一步评估了3D人类下游任务的生成点云估计。 我们显示,在生成的人体LiDAR样本上预先训练一个姿势估计器,然后对真实数据进行微调,大大提高了完整数据和低数据系统的表现。 实训集分数不一的实验进一步表明,我们生成的数据可以弥补贴有标签的有限实训数据.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are:
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献是:

blocks.en: • We introduce HuLiGen , to the best of our knowledge, the first learned generative mapping from parametric human body models to LiDAR point-clouds, learning real LiDAR characteristics. • We demonstrate the practical value of the learned LiDAR distribution through downstream 3D HPE. Pretraining on generated human LiDAR observations followed by finetuning on real data reduces MPJPE from 6.02 cm to 5.04 cm on SLOPER4D and from 6.74 cm to 5.85 cm on WOD, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both datasets. • We demonstrate strong gains in the low-annotation setting on WOD, where our pretraining pipeline reduces MPJPE by about 50% using only 1% and 10% of the available pose annotations. • We further show that our pretraining pipeline remains effective in low-data settings, reducing MPJPE by about 30% and 25% on SLOPER4D [ 7 ] , and by 42% and 36% on WOD [ 39 ] , when using only 10% and 20% of the real training data, respectively.

blocks.en: 2 Related works
blocks.zh: 2 相关作品

blocks.en:
Lidar-based human pose estimation is challenging due to the sparsity, non-uniform density and partial observation of the human body. Early approaches therefore focused on extracting more structured representations from sparse measurements. LidPose [ 17 ] projects human point clouds into structured 2D representations, LPFormer [ 45 ] combines BEV and sparse voxel features, and VoxelKP [ 37 ] operates directly on high-resolution sparse voxels.
LiDAR-HMR [ 8 ] leverages Pose Regression Network (PRN) to estimate 3D keypoints directly from human LiDAR point clouds through probabilistic point-wise voting and attention-based refinement.
Other works compensate for missing geometric information using complementary cues: MMVP [ 9 ] and HUM3DIL [ 46 ] fuse RGB and LiDAR information, while LiDAR-HMP [ 12 ] exploits temporal context. More recently, the focus has shifted toward learning stronger human-specific representations. UniPVU-Human [ 42 ] learns body-part and motion priors before downstream pose estimation, while DAPT [ 3 ] explicitly addresses variations in LiDAR point density through density-aware feature learning. Beyond architectural improvements, GC-KPL [ 40 ] tackles the limited availability of labeled LiDAR data by combining synthetic pretraining with geometric and temporal self-supervision on unlabeled real data.
blocks.zh:
以利达为主的人体姿势估计由于人体的痉挛性,非统一密度和部分观察而具有挑战性. 因此,早期方法的重点是从稀少的测量中提取更有条理的表述。 LidPose [17] 将人类点云分为结构化的2D表示法,LPFormer [45] 结合了BEV和稀有的花瓶特征,而VoxelKP [37] 直接在高分辨率的稀有花瓶上运行.
LiDAR-HMR [8] 杠杆 Pose回放网络(PRN)通过概率点位的投票和基于注意力的完善,直接从人类的LiDAR点子云中估算出3D键点.
其他作品利用互补提示来弥补缺失的几何信息:MMVP [9]和HUM3DIL [46] 引信RGB和LiDAR信息,而LiDAR-HMP [12]则利用了时间背景. 最近,重点已转向学习更强有力的针对具体人类的表述。 UniPVU-Human [42]在下游提出估计之前先学习身体部位和运动前科,而DAPT [3]则通过密度-意识特征的学习明确解决了LiDAR点密度的变化. 除了建筑改进外,GC-KPL[40]还解决了贴有标签的LiDAR数据的有限可用性问题,将合成预训与无标签真实数据上的几何和时间自监督相结合。

blocks.en:
Beyond developing better architectures and representations, prior work has also attempted to address the scarcity of annotated human LiDAR data. One line of research introduces additional supervision from images, using 2D annotations or pseudo-labels together with LiDAR to reduce the dependence on 3D pose labels [ 11 , 48 , 4 , 6 , 29 ] . For LiDAR-only methods, two strategies are commonly adopted to increase training diversity and quantity. VoxelKP [ 37 ] , LPFormer [ 45 ] , and LidPose [ 17 ] rely on extensive data augmentation, such as frustum dropout, frame mixing, body cropping and geometric transformations, to perturb existing real samples.
A second direction generates entirely new LiDAR observations from parametric human models using simulated LiDAR ray casting and hand-designed perturbations, such as laser-level masks for occlusion [ 3 , 40 , 35 , 42 ] .
This makes it possible to exploit large-scale body-model repositories such as AMASS [ 24 ] , even though they do not contain paired LiDAR measurements. In contrast, our approach preserves this ability to leverage large-scale human body data while learning the mapping from body models to LiDAR observations directly from real data.
blocks.zh:
除了发展更好的架构和表述外,先前的工作还试图解决附加说明的人类LiDAR数据的稀缺问题。 一行研究引入了从图像中的额外监督,使用2D说明或伪标签同LiDAR一起来减少对3D平面标签的依赖[11,48,4,6,29]. 对于只使用LiDAR的方法,通常采用两种战略来增加培训的多样性和数量. VoxelKP [37],LPFormer [45],和LidPose [17] 依靠广泛的数据增强,如frustum display,帧相混合,身体收割和几何变换,以扰动现有的真实样本.
第二个方向是利用模拟的LiDAR射线铸造和手设计的扰动,从参数人类模型中产生全新的LiDAR观测结果,例如用于闭塞的激光级口罩[3,40,35,42].
这使得有可能利用AMAS[24]等大型体型库,尽管它们并不包含配对的LiDAR测量. 相形之下,我们的方法保留了利用大型人体数据的能力,同时直接从真实数据中学习从身体模型到LiDAR观测的绘图.

blocks.en:
Lidar point cloud generation. LiDAR generation has evolved from raycasting simulators in virtual environments [ 10 ] to learned generative models based on energy functions, discrete latents and diffusion [ 49 , 41 , 27 , 31 ] . Most of these methods, however, focus on full-scene generation rather than the fidelity of individual objects.
Recent object-level LiDAR generators explicitly model foreground objects. These methods generate localized objects with diffusion, using conditioning such as object class, position, or viewpoint, and can integrate the generated instances back into complete driving scenes [ 43 , 16 ] .
Despite this progress, existing LiDAR generators are not designed to generate humans conditioned on their underlying body pose and shape.
blocks.zh:
利达点云生成. LiDAR的生成已经从虚拟环境中的射线模拟器[10]发展到基于能函数,离散潜伏和扩散的已学会的基因模型[49,41,27,31]. 然而,这些方法大多注重于全色的生成,而不是单个物体的忠诚.
近期对象级的LiDAR生成器明确为模型前地对象. 这些方法利用对象类,位置,或视角等条件,生成具有扩散性的局部物体,并可以将所生成的实例回放到完整的驱动场景 [43, 16].
尽管取得了这些进步,但现有的LiDAR发电机的设计并不能够产生以基本身体外形和外形为条件的人类.

blocks.en: Our goal is to learn to predict how a LiDAR would capture a human, as represented by a parametric body model. Formally, given a human point cloud 𝐏 \mathbf{P} and its corresponding body model 𝐁 \mathbf{B} , we want to learn the conditional distribution p ⁡ ( 𝐏 ∣ 𝐁 ) , \displaystyle p(\mathbf{P}\mid\mathbf{B}), (1) where 𝐁 \mathbf{B} can be further decomposed into [ 𝐨 , β , θ ] [\mathbf{o},\beta,\theta] the oriented location of the subject, the body shape and local body pose representations respectively.
blocks.zh: 我们的目标是学习如何预测一个LiDAR会如何捕捉一个人类,以一个参数体模型为代表. 形式上,鉴于人点云 P\mathbf{P}及其对应的身体型号 B\mathbf{B},我们希望学习有条件的分布 p\\ (P \ \ B ),\ displaystyle p (\mathbf{P \ mid\ mathb{B}), (1) B\mathb{B}可以进一步分解为 [o, β, θ [\ mathbf{o},\beta,\theta] 对象的方向位置,身体形状和地方身体分别呈现出代表.

blocks.en: We model this conditional distribution using flow matching (FM) parametrized by a neural network operating directly on the 3D point cloud. Starting from a random Gaussian point cloud, this flow-matching model learns to gradually move the 3D points towards that of a human LiDAR capture, conditionally to [ 𝐨 , β , θ ] [\mathbf{o},\beta,\theta] that correspond to the body model 𝐁 \mathbf{B} of the human. Because each LiDAR produces very different distributions of point clouds, we train a separate model for each acquisition setting so that sensor-dependent characteristics are captured independently.
blocks.zh: 我们利用直接在3D点云上运行的神经网络对流配对(FM)进行参数化模拟这种有条件的分布. 从随机高斯点云开始,这个流相比模型学习了将3D点逐渐移向人类的LiDAR捕获点上,有条件地向[o,β,θ] [\mathbf{o},\β,\theta] 对应人类的身体模型B\mathbf{B}. 因为每个LiDAR会产生非常不同的点云分布,所以我们为每个获取设置培训一个单独的模型,这样可以独立地捕捉到传感器依赖的特性.

blocks.en: 3.2 Human-centric parameterization

blocks.en: Because humans are articulated and their capture by a LiDAR results in very local interactions, the choice of coordinate system is crucial to provide relevant information to the flow-matching model. blocks.en: Our conditioning 𝐁 \mathbf{B} combines three complementary sources of information: ( ϕ rel , ρ , z ⏟ oriented body location ​ 𝐨 , β ⏟ body shape , θ ⏟ local body pose ) , \Big(\underbrace{\phi_{\mathrm{rel}},\rho,z}_{\text{oriented body location }\mathbf{o}},\,\underbrace{\beta\vphantom{\phi_{\mathrm{rel}}}}_{\text{body shape}},\,\underbrace{\theta\vphantom{\phi_{\mathrm{rel}}}}_{\text{local body pose}}\Big), (6) that require specific encoding each.

Because angular variables are discontinuous at − π -\pi and π \pi , we first represent ϕ rel \phi_{\mathrm{rel}} through its sine and cosine components and apply a cyclic embedding. The radial distance ρ \rho and height z z are represented using Fourier features. This provides 3 sensor-related condition tokens.

Using the parametric body model for the shape, each of the shape coefficients is independently embedded into a different token using an MLP to keep these parameters disentangled, leading to different condition tokens.

blocks.en: Using the body model for the pose θ \theta , we convert the axis-angle to 3D cartesian coordinates using forward kinematics and embed each of the 3D body joints using a PointNet [ 30 ] model to obtain one token per joint. To retain the semantic information of the joints, we keep their order the same and add a learned positional encoding.

blocks.en: The condition encoding results in the concatenation of all the tokens in a single sequence of tokens.

blocks.en:
To retain the characteristic of each LiDAR setup, we train separate models for different datasets.
In the following experiments, we use a modified DiT-XS/4 configuration from [ 16 ] , with 12 transformer blocks, a hidden dimension of 192, and three attention heads.
blocks.zh:
为了保留每个LiDAR设置的特征,我们为不同的数据集培训单独的模型.
在接下来的实验中,我们使用从 [16] 开始的经过修改的 DiT-XS/4 配置,其中12个变压器块,隐藏的维度为192,并有3个注意头.

blocks.en:
We train FM models for 200 epochs with a batch size of 128 and a learning rate of 1e-4. To handle variable-size point clouds, we pad each sample to the maximum number of points within the batch. For generation, we follow [ 23 ] and solve the corresponding ordinary differential equation using the Euler solver with 50 sampling steps.
All models are trained on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU and take roughly 15 and 3 hours to train on SLOPER4D and WOD, respectively.
blocks.zh:
我们为200个纪元培训调频模型,批量尺寸为128个,学习率为1e-4. 为了处理可变大小的点云,我们把每个样本放入批内的最大点数. 对于生成,我们遵循[23],并使用有50个采样步骤的欧拉解析器来解析相应的普通微分方程.
所有型号都经过了单一NVIDIA H200 GPU的训练,并分别用了大约15和3小时在SLOPER4D和WOD上进行训练.

blocks.en: We conduct experiments on SLOPER4D [ 7 ] and the Waymo Open Dataset (WOD) [ 39 ] . SLOPER4D is an outdoor human motion-capture dataset containing synchronized LiDAR point clouds and RGB images, with ground-truth human meshes and 3D keypoints obtained using motion-capture devices. Since the dataset does not provide an official train/test split, we follow LiDAR-HMR [ 8 ] and use 24,9k samples for training and 8,1k samples for testing.
blocks.zh: 我们进行SLOPER4D[7]和Waymo Open Datas集的实验[39]. SLOPER4D是一款室外人类动作捕捉数据集,包含同步的LiDAR点云和RGB图像,并有地-真人网和用动作捕捉装置得到的3D键. 由于数据集没有提供正式的列车/测试分出,我们跟随LiDAR-HMR[8],使用24,9k的样本进行培训,并使用8,1k的样本进行测试.

blocks.en:
For WOD, we use the human keypoint annotations provided with the v2.0 release, containing 8,1k annotated human instances for training and 1,8k for testing.
As WOD does not provide ground-truth human meshes, we adopt the pseudo-mesh annotations from [ 8 ] .
blocks.zh:
对WOD来说,我们使用在v2.0发行时提供的人类键标说明,包含8,1k个注解的人类实例用于培训,1,8k用于测试.
由于WOD不提供地表真人膜,我们采纳了 [8] 的伪地膜说明.

blocks.en: We evaluate generation quality on the validation set of each dataset using both sample-level and distribution-level metrics.
blocks.zh: 我们使用抽样和分布级的衡量标准,对每个数据集的验证组进行生成质量评价。

blocks.en: We measure the geometric similarity between a generated point cloud and the real observation with the same conditioning input using the Chamfer Distance (CD).
blocks.zh: 我们用Chamfer距离(CD)测量生成的点云与使用相同条件输入的实际观测之间的几何相似性。

blocks.en: We assess distributional realism using the Fréchet PointNet Distance (FPD) [ 38 ] , adapted from FID [ 13 ] . We extract point-cloud representations from the PRN network [ 8 ] , using the features after its final multi-head self-attention layer and before the FCN head. We train a separate PRN for each dataset. We similarly adapt the Kernel Inception Distance (KID) [ 5 ] , which is particularly suitable for smaller sample sets, and denote the resulting metric as Kernel PointNet Distance (KPD).
blocks.zh: 我们使用Fréchet PointNet距离(FPD)[38],根据FID[13]进行分配现实主义评估。 我们从PRN网络中提取出点-云表示[8],使用其最终多头自留层后和FCN头前的特征. 我们为每个数据集训练一个单独的PRN. 我们同样也适应了Kernel Inception距离(KID)[5],这特别适用于更小的样本集,并且表示由此得出的度量标准为Kernel PointNet距离(KPD).

blocks.en:
Finally, we compare the real and generated point-cloud distributions using coverage (COV) [ 1 ] and nearest-neighbor accuracy (1-NNA) [ 44 , 22 ] following [ 26 ] , computed using CD.
COV measures how much of the real distribution is covered by generated samples, while 1-NNA measures how easily real and generated samples can be separated using nearest neighbors. A 1-NNA of 50 % 50\% indicates indistinguishable distributions.
blocks.zh:
最后,我们用覆盖面(COV)[1]和最近的准确度(1-NNA)[44,22]来比较使用光盘计算的实际和产生的点-云分布。
COV测量实际分布中有多少被生成的样品所覆盖,而1-NNA测量如何利用最近的相邻地区来方便地分离真实和生成的样品. 1-NNA为50%-50\%表示无法区分的分布.

blocks.en:
To demonstrate the practical impact of our method, we use our trained FM models to generate new human LiDAR observations from poses in the AMASS database [ 24 ] . Specifically, we use KIT and HumanEva sequences and filter them to walking , standing and running , resulting in 47,494 unique body poses.
We sample the local body pose from AMASS, while bootstrapping the global body orientated location, shape and target point count from the target dataset, i.e., SLOPER4D or WOD. This places novel poses in realistic target-domain observation settings and allows the generator to produce realistic point densities and off-surface structures, rather than being limited to the returns obtained from ray casting a bare body mesh.
This provides a source of synthetic LiDAR samples with corresponding 3D keypoint annotations.
We then pretrain a LiDAR-based 3D human pose estimator on the generated data, using the publicly available PRN [ 8 ] as the downstream model. In a second stage, we finetune the pretrained PRN on real LiDAR data. We illustrate this pipeline in Fig. 3 .
In both stages, we train PRN using 15 keypoints for 50 epochs using the Adam optimizer, with a batch size of 64 and a learning rate of 5e-4.
We evaluate downstream performance using MPJPE and PA-MPJPE, reported in centimeters; in the tables, PA denotes PA-MPJPE.
blocks.zh:
为了展示我们的方法的实际影响,我们利用我们训练有素的调频模型,从AMASS数据库中的平面产生新的人类LiDAR观测. [24]. 具体来说,我们使用KIT和HumanEva序列并过滤它们来行走,站立和跑动,从而形成47,494个独特的身体姿势.
我们从AMASS中取出当地身体的样本,同时从目标数据集,即SLOPER4D或WOD中,将全球身体定位、形状和目标点计数拖住。 这使得新事物在现实的目标域观测设置中呈现出,使生成者能够产生现实的点密度和地外结构,而不是局限于从射线铸出裸体网所得到的回报.
这提供了合成LiDAR样本的来源,并附有相应的3D关键点说明.
然后我们用公开的PRN[8]作为下游模型,在生成的数据上预先培养出一个基于LiDAR的3D的人类外形估计器. 在第二阶段,我们根据真实的LiDAR数据来微调预训的PRN. 我们在图3中说明了这个管道。
在这两个阶段中,我们使用15个键点来训练PRN,用于使用亚当优化器的50个纪元,批量尺寸为64个,学习率为5e-4.
我们使用PPJPE和PA-MPJPE评估下游的业绩,以厘米计;在表格中,PA表示PA-MPJPE。

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental analysis
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验分析

blocks.en: Since SLOPER4D provides ground-truth human meshes, we conduct our ablation experiments on this dataset and report the generative quality metrics on the validation set. We begin with a simple setup without canonical coordinate transformation, conditioning only on the body pose θ \theta while discarding the shape parameter β \beta . As shown in Tab. 1 , both canonical transformation and shape conditioning improve performance when introduced separately and combining them yields further gains. Finally, replacing the angular pose with joint coordinates obtained through forward kinematics achieves the best performance.
blocks.zh: 由于SLOPER4D提供地基真实的人类网格,我们在此数据集上进行消融实验,并在验证集上报告基因质量计量. 我们从一个简单的设置开始,没有犬形坐标变换, 仅在身体上摆出\\theta, 同时丢弃形状参数β\β。 如表1所显示的,在分别采用和合并时,犬形变换和形状调节都会提高性能,从而产生进一步的收益。 最后,取而代之的是角姿势,取而代之的是通过前向运动器获得的联合坐标,从而达到最佳的性能.

blocks.en: We also compare our generated samples against a raycasting baseline. For this baseline, we raycast the meshes from the corresponding validation sets using the respective LiDAR sensor specifications: 64 beams with a 20 ∘ 20^{\circ} vertical FoV for WOD and 128 beams with a 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} vertical FoV for SLOPER4D. As shown in Tab. 4 , our generated point clouds achieve better generative quality.

We provide additional details regarding our method and ablations in the supplementary material.

在表2中,我们还汇报了WOD上我们最后模型的基因质量衡量标准,并与射线基线进行比较。 与SLOPER4D的结果一致,我们的模型实现了更好的总体基因质量.
我们提供了补充材料中我们的方法和细节。

blocks.en: We further evaluate the quality and practical utility of our generated samples on downstream LiDAR-based 3D human pose estimation. We first pretrain PRN on our generated human LiDAR data and then finetune the pretrained model on real human LiDAR instances. The results are summarized in Tab. 3 . For both datasets, pretraining consistently outperforms training from scratch across different synthetic pretraining set sizes, and performance further improves as the amount of generated data increases. We compare our pretraining pipeline using HuLiGen -generated samples against existing LiDAR-based 3D HPE methods on the validation sets of WOD and SLOPER4D in Tab. 5 , with qualitative results shown in Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 . For a fair comparison, we primarily consider methods that do not rely on additional large-scale real-world training datasets. In particular, DAPT [ 3 ] additionally uses LiDARHuman26M [ 18 ] , which contains 184K LiDAR frames. For SLOPER4D, some mesh-reconstruction methods do not explicitly report MPJPE. For these methods, we compute MPJPE from joints obtained from their predicted pose, shape and translation parameters to allow a consistent comparison.

blocks.en: 4.3 Low-annotation regime
blocks.zh: 4.3 低说明制度

blocks.en:
Our approach can be particularly useful when LiDAR data is abundant but only a small fraction is annotated with 3D human keypoints.
We investigate this on WOD, where ground-truth meshes are unavailable and the body models are instead obtained using an off-the-shelf estimator [ 8 ] .
We use the full training set to learn our FM model, generate ∼ \sim 48k human LiDAR samples from AMASS, and pretrain PRN on these samples. We then finetune PRN using only 1 % 1\% or 10 % 10\% of the labeled training data.
As shown in Tab. 6 , this reduces the error by more than 50% compared with training from scratch when using only 1 % 1\% and 10 % 10\% of the annotations. It also outperforms the raycasting baselines and GC-KPL [ 40 ] in both low-annotation settings.

blocks.en:
The other challenging setting where HuLiGen can be particularly effective is the low-data regime, where only a limited amount of real LiDAR data is available, rather than merely limited annotations.
To simulate this scenario, we restrict the entire pipeline to only 10 % 10\% and 20 % 20\% of the available real data. We first train the FM model on the corresponding low-data subset and use it to generate ∼ \sim 48k synthetic human LiDAR samples from AMASS. We then pretrain the pose estimator on these generated samples and, in the final stage, finetune it using the same limited fraction of real data.
As shown in Tab. 7 , our pipeline substantially improves over training from scratch, reducing MPJPE and PA-MPJPE by approximately 30 % 30\% on SLOPER4D and 45 % 45\% on WOD. These results further demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach when real LiDAR data itself is scarce.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduced HuLiGen , a point-transformer-based flow-matching model for human LiDAR generation conditioned on parametric body models. HuLiGen produces more realistic observations than standard raycasting and allows large pose repositories to be converted into synthetic LiDAR data. We show that pretraining HPE on these samples significantly improves performance, with particularly strong gains in low-data and low-annotation regimes.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们引入了HuLiGen,一种以参数体模型为条件的用于人类LiDAR生成的以点转换为基流相匹配的模型. HuLiGen产生比标准射线显示更现实的观测结果,并允许将大型外形寄存器转换为合成的LiDAR数据. 我们显示,在这些样本上预先训练高专能能显著地提高性能,在低数据和低注释制度上特别有显著的收获.
